summary.name: 10 Years of Crashing Google
summary.one_liner: A LISA 2015 conference talk by Google's Kripa Krishnan on a decade of intentionally causing failures in Google's systems to find and fix them early.
use_cases: Learning how Google deliberately triggers failures to find weaknesses
Building incident response and postmortem processes
Background reading on chaos engineering history
summary.what_it_does: The talk describes Google's long-standing practice of deliberately causing failures in its own systems so they can be found and fixed before they happen uncontrolled. It covers supporting components built around this practice: failure automation, incident response, learning from postmortems, and failure prevention. The speaker presents learnings and war stories from across the whole lifecycle. The speaker, Kripa Krishnan, has led Google's Disaster Recovery Program (DiRT) for about nine years. The page itself is a conference session listing with an abstract and speaker bio.
notable: Covers Google's DiRT disaster recovery program experience over about a decade
Talk from USENIX LISA 2015 in Washington, D.C.
Papers and post-event slides/video are openly accessible per USENIX Open Access policy
caveats: Page is a session abstract; the full talk content is not on the page text itself
Only a summary of topics is given, no specific tools or methods named
